periods.analysis: We are starting this sequence from a strong green baseline: Overall Resident Satisfaction is 4.24 on a 1-5 scale against the >=4 target, with no prior quarter for comparison in this reporting run. The Q3 pulse survey drew solid coverage across the Bayside, North Harbor, and Ridgeview cohorts, and the data team completed duplicate-response cleanup before the council packet cutoff. Comments were especially favorable on library programming, summer parks activation, and the new HarborConnect service-request confirmations, which gives departments credit for visible follow-through. This is a healthy opening marker for a fast-growing city, and it tells us residents are still feeling the value of core services even as demand rises.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green result by keeping the Q4 survey calendar locked: launch resident reminders in weeks 2 and 5, and keep department response-owner lists current in HarborConnect. Extend what worked by packaging one-page service highlights from Parks, Library, and 311 for council and neighborhood association distribution. Ask each department to submit two resident-facing improvements by the next reporting deadline so we can connect satisfaction movement to concrete actions.

periods.analysis: Satisfaction remains green at 4.18, down -0.06 from 4.24 in 2024-Q3, which is a modest seasonal softening rather than a structural concern. The dip lines up with higher winter call volume on permit inspections, holiday parking enforcement, and storm-drain cleanup routes along Seacliff and Marina Loop. Data quality held up well: the Communications team verified Spanish, Vietnamese, and English survey samples before close, which keeps the story reliable for council. Even with the quarter-over-quarter decline, the score is still comfortably above the >=4 target and reflects a community that remains broadly satisfied.
periods.recommendations: Sustain performance by continuing multilingual survey outreach and adding a short “you said, we did” insert to Q1 utility bills. Extend service visibility by having Community Development publish weekly permit queue snapshots during January and February, when inspection expectations are highest. Watch the parking and storm-response comment tags specifically, and bring a short exception report if either topic rises above the agreed 12% share of open-ended comments.

periods.analysis: Q1 rebounds to 4.29, up +0.11 from 4.18 in 2024-Q4, which puts the measure firmly back on an upward line while staying green. The improvement coincides with the January “First 100 Days of Service” campaign, faster 311 closure messaging, and the permit counter’s Tuesday/Thursday express lanes for small residential projects. The resident panel also had stronger participation from renters near Harbor Station, a cohort we specifically needed to hear from as transit-oriented development accelerates. My read for council is straightforward: departments responded to Q4 friction points, and residents noticed.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the gain by keeping the express permit lanes through Q2 and tracking same-day completion separately from standard plan reviews. Extend HarborConnect closure messaging to Parks work orders, especially playground repairs and field-light requests, so residents see the same feedback loop across departments. Before the next reporting cycle, refresh the renter panel list with property managers at Harbor Station, Tide Flats, and East Pier to protect sample balance.

periods.analysis: Satisfaction rises again to 4.31, up +0.02 from 4.29 in 2025-Q1, keeping the measure green and above the >=4 target. The smaller movement is still meaningful because Q2 included heavier beach-season preparation, special-event permitting, and school-year traffic coordination around the Shoreline Avenue corridor. Departments looked coordinated: Public Works published construction detour maps for Route 14 resurfacing, Parks opened the summer field reservation desk on time, and Police expanded weekend waterfront ambassadors. This quarter shows Harborview can absorb growth and seasonal pressure without eroding resident confidence.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green by repeating the Q2 interdepartmental readiness huddle every April, with Transportation, Parks, Police, Fire, and Communications all confirming resident-facing milestones. Extend the detour-map practice to all capital projects over 10 working days, using a standard template and QR code signage at project limits. For Q3, add a brief event-permit satisfaction question so we can separate general resident sentiment from applicant experience.

periods.analysis: Q3 posts 4.3, down -0.01 from 4.31 in 2025-Q2, which is essentially flat and remains green. That tiny movement came during Harborview’s busiest visitor period, including Marina Nights, youth sports tournaments at Gull Point, and expanded weekend trash routes on the waterfront. The open-ended comments show residents appreciated the visible service presence, particularly the blue-shirt ambassador teams and the added receptacle pickups on Pier 2 and Beachwalk. I would not over-read the -0.01 change, but I do want us to keep the operational proof points tight because council will rightly ask how we maintain satisfaction at this growth pace.
periods.recommendations: Sustain performance by carrying the ambassador staffing model into the first three weekends of Q4, then documenting costs and resident contacts by location. Extend weekend waterfront trash route data into a public dashboard tile so the service level is visible, not just delivered. Keep the Q4 survey instrument unchanged except for one optional comment prompt on visitor-season impacts, so the quarter-over-quarter comparison stays clean.

periods.analysis: Satisfaction is 4.27, down -0.03 from 4.3 in 2025-Q3, still green and still clearly above the >=4 target. The quarter included expected winter stressors: early storms, end-of-year permit rushes, and a higher number of utility and streetlight inquiries routed through HarborConnect. The decline is manageable, and the resident comments suggest the issue is more about timeliness of status updates than dissatisfaction with final outcomes. Importantly, departments met the reporting deadline with complete narrative notes, which helps us give council a candid but confident account.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green result by requiring status-update timestamps on all HarborConnect cases open longer than seven calendar days. Extend the Q4 communications playbook by pre-writing storm, streetlight, and permit-delay message templates before the next winter cycle. Ask Public Works and Community Development to bring one queue-reduction action each to the January performance check-in, with owner and due date assigned.

Sustain the improvement by keeping the seven-day HarborConnect prompt active and reviewing overdue-case aging at every monthly operating meeting. Extend Saturday ADU appointments through Q2, but cap each session at 18 bookings so staff can maintain service quality. Prepare a council-ready appendix that links resident satisfaction comments to the specific operational changes made since 2025-Q4.

periods.analysis:
Q2 resident satisfaction reached 4.34, up 0.03 points from 4.31 in Q1 and the strongest result in the eight-quarter trend. The improvement occurred during peak spring construction, early beach operations, and expanded recreation registration, indicating that service delivery remained steady amid elevated seasonal demand. Residents responded positively to more timely and accessible service information, including capital-project QR signage, recreation waitlist texts, and the permit/inspection dashboard launched in May. 
 Despite this positive measure-level trend, the measure and its parent objective remain in Caution status, while the linked Smart City Digital Services Initiative is On Target. This suggests the satisfaction gain is encouraging but has not yet translated into sufficient confidence at the broader community-outcome level.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green by formalizing the service-update standards into a citywide resident communications checklist for every department by the next quarterly close. Extend the permit/inspection dashboard to include average turnaround by application type, starting with ADUs, tenant improvements, and small commercial remodels. For the next cycle, keep the survey fielding window and methodology stable so the 4.34 result remains comparable and defensible.

periods.analysis: September satisfaction is 3.98, up from 3.94 in June but still below the 4.00 target. Survey fielding has closed; the November Council briefing is the opportunity to explain the result without treating a small improvement as target attainment.
periods.recommendations: Validate the respondent mix and bring the survey findings and practical service improvements to the Council briefing.
